statement: Let $G$ be a connected simply connected semisimple group over an algebraically closed field, $P\subseteq G$ a parabolic subgroup, and $X_w\subseteq G/P$ a Schubert variety. For a dominant character $\lambda$ of $P$, with the convention that $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ is globally generated, one has \[ H^i(X_w,\mathcal L(\lambda)|_{X_w})=0\quad(i>0), \] and restriction $H^0(G/P,\mathcal L(\lambda))\to H^0(X_w,\mathcal L(\lambda)|_{X_w})$ is surjective. In particular every nef line bundle on the complete homogeneous space $G/P$ has vanishing higher cohomology. This holds in every characteristic.
where_proved: sections/part_b.tex, label thm:B3-homogeneous, statement 8.37, PDF p. 87
notes: Complete homogeneous spaces; arbitrary homogeneous spaces not asserted Task aliases: B.3.20. Contributor status detail: Known with checked deduction.

statement: Let $X$ be noetherian and $F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. Parshin--Beilinson ad\`eles give a functorial flasque resolution \[ 0\longrightarrow F\longrightarrow\mathbb A^0(F) \longrightarrow\mathbb A^1(F)\longrightarrow\cdots. \] Consequently the alternating flag complex of global ad\`eles computes $H^*(X,F)$. If $X$ is also reduced, excellent and pure dimensional of dimension $n$, the ad\`ele ring of a saturated length-$n$ flag is a finite product of $n$-local fields with last residue fields finite over the residue field of the final point. For the local-Jacobian part, let $A$ be noetherian, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $\mathfrak C=\operatorname{Spf}A[[T]]$, and $U=\operatorname{Spec}A((T))$. The commutative group functor \[ \mathcal J(R)=R((T))^\times \] on $A$-algebras has a canonical natural bijection \[ \operatorname{Hom}_{S\text{-}\mathrm{gp}}(\mathcal J,G) \simeq G(U) \] for every smooth separated commutative $S$-group scheme $G$. It is implemented by an Abel--Jacobi morphism $U\to\mathcal J_{\rm omb}$ and the canonical extensions of group homomorphisms to this intermediate functor. It is not implemented by a morphism $U\to\mathcal J$.
where_proved: sections/part_b.tex, label thm:B3-adeles, statement 8.38, PDF p. 88
notes: Local Jacobian universal bijection is mediated by ombre functor, not U to loop group Task aliases: B.3.27. Contributor status detail: Known with checked deduction.

statement: Let $X$ be a complex analytic manifold of dimension $d$, countable at infinity, and $\mathcal D_X$ its sheaf of holomorphic differential operators. For every bounded complex $M$ of left $\mathcal D_X$-modules with holonomic cohomology, put \[ \mathrm{DR}(M)=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal D_X}(\mathcal O_X,M), \qquad \mathrm{Sol}(M)=R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal D_X}(M,\mathcal O_X). \] There is a canonical isomorphism \[ \mathrm{DR}(M)\simeq R\mathcal Hom_{\C_X}(\mathrm{Sol}(M),\C_X). \] Equivalently, with Verdier duality $D_X(-)=R\mathcal Hom_{\C_X}(-,\C_X[2d])$, one has \[ \mathrm{DR}(M)[d]\simeq D_X(\mathrm{Sol}(M)[d]). \] No regular-singularity assumption is required for this local duality.
where_proved: sections/part_b.tex, label thm:B3-dmodule, statement 8.39, PDF p. 89
notes: No regular-singularity hypothesis; analytic and crystalline statements kept distinct Task aliases: B.3.8.duality. Contributor status detail: Known with checked deduction.

statement: For every separated finite type scheme $X$ over a field there is a Riemann--Roch transformation \[ \tau_X:G_0(X)\longrightarrow\mathrm{CH}_*(X)_\Q \] commuting with proper pushforward and satisfying $\tau_X(E\otimes F)=\operatorname{ch}(E)\cap\tau_X(F)$ for vector bundles $E$. If $X$ is smooth, then $\tau_X(F)=\operatorname{ch}(F)\operatorname{td}(T_X)\cap[X]$. Thus for a proper morphism $f:X\to Y$ of smooth schemes, \[ f_*\bigl(\operatorname{ch}(E)\operatorname{td}(T_X)\cap[X]\bigr) =\operatorname{ch}(Rf_*E)\operatorname{td}(T_Y)\cap[Y]. \] Neither $X,Y$ nor $f$ is required to be projective. For proper pseudo-coherent morphisms of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes, $Rf_*$ preserves pseudo-coherent complexes. If the morphism also has finite Tor dimension, it preserves perfect complexes. This includes proper lci morphisms and nonnoetherian bases. For complex analytic spaces, coherent sheaves likewise have a natural transformation $\alpha_X:G_0^{\rm hol}(X)\to K^{\rm top}_0(X)$ to topological $K$-homology, compatible with proper direct images. On a complex manifold it sends a vector bundle to its Dolbeault $K$-homology class. This includes possibly singular and nonprojective complex spaces.
where_proved: sections/part_b.tex, label thm:B3-riemann-roch, statement 8.40, PDF p. 89

statement: Let $S$ be locally noetherian with G-ring local rings, and let $\mathcal X$ be a category fibred in groupoids over $S$ satisfying the usual set-size condition. Suppose its diagonal is representable by algebraic spaces, it is an \'etale stack, and it commutes with filtered limits of affine schemes. Suppose also that its deformation categories satisfy the Rim--Schlessinger fibre-product condition and have finite dimensional tangent and infinitesimal-automorphism spaces, every formal object over a complete noetherian local $S$-algebra is effective, and versality is open in finite type families. Then $\mathcal X$ is an algebraic stack, locally of finite presentation over $S$.
where_proved: sections/part_b.tex, label thm:B3-stacks, statement 8.41, PDF p. 90
notes: Effectiveness, openness of versality and finite deformation spaces are substantive hypotheses Task aliases: B.3.14.stacks. Contributor status detail: Known with checked deduction.

statement: Let $R\rightrightarrows U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be an equivalence relation of schemes with both projections finite locally free. Write $R=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and \[ C=\{a\in A:s^*a=t^*a\text{ in }B\}. \] Then the fppf quotient is the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}C$, $U\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is finite faithfully flat, and $R=U\times_{\operatorname{Spec}C}U$. In particular this applies to artinian $U$; its quotient is again artinian. The same conclusion of schematic representability holds for nonaffine $U$ if every equivalence class is contained in an affine open, as is the case for $U$ quasi-projective over an affine scheme.
where_proved: sections/part_b.tex, label thm:B3-artinian, statement 8.42, PDF p. 91
notes: Schematic nonaffine extension when every orbit has affine neighbourhood; quasiprojective only over affine base Task aliases: B.3.18.artinian. Contributor status detail: Known with checked deduction.

statement: Let $X$ be a compact complex manifold, $E$ a holomorphic vector bundle, $f:X\to X$ holomorphic, and $u:f^*E\to E$ a holomorphic bundle map. Suppose every fixed point $x$ is nondegenerate: $\det_\C(1-df_x)\ne0$. Then the induced maps on coherent cohomology satisfy \[ \sum_q(-1)^q\operatorname{Tr}(u\circ f^*:H^q(X,E)) =\sum_{f(x)=x}\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(u_x)} {\det_\C(1-df_x)}. \] More generally an elliptic complex on a compact smooth manifold, with a geometric endomorphism over a map having only nondegenerate fixed points, has local contribution $\sum_q(-1)^q\operatorname{Tr}(u_{q,x})/ |\det_\R(1-df_x)|$.
where_proved: sections/part_b.tex, label thm:B3-holomorphic-lefschetz, statement 8.43, PDF p. 91
notes: Compact manifold; nondegenerate isolated fixed points; denominator and complex trace derived Task aliases: B.3.6.coherent. Contributor status detail: Known with checked deduction.

statement: Every $\infty$-topos $\mathcal X$ has a shape, the pro-space corepresenting the accessible left exact functor $K\mapsto\Gamma_{\mathcal X}(\Delta K)$. A pointed object $A\in\mathcal X$ has internal homotopy sheaves $\pi_n(A)=\tau_{\leq0}\Omega^nA$; fibre sequences give the usual long exact sequence, with the group action interpretation at $\pi_0$. If $A$ is $(n-1)$-connected and $n\geq1$, then \[ \pi_n(A)^{\mathrm{ab}}\otimes M \simeq\widetilde H_n(A;M) \] for every internal abelian group $M$. For a finite type $\C$-scheme $X$, the profinite completion of its \'etale shape is the profinite completion of the singular homotopy type of $X^{\rm an}$. Infinitesimal homotopy sheaves are possible on the fppf site: in characteristic $p$, $B\alpha_p$ has $\pi_1=\alpha_p$. They are not detected by the small \emph{\'etale} site of a reduced scheme. The distinction between internal homotopy sheaves and external pro-homotopy groups of the shape is essential.
where_proved: sections/part_b.tex, label thm:B3-homotopy, statement 8.44, PDF p. 92
depends_on: Lurie 6.5.1/7.1.6; Christensen-Scoccola Thm3.12; SGA1 XII5.1; SGA4 XVI4.1;source:BLurieHTT;source:BChristensenScoccola;source:BSGA1;source:BSGA4XVI
notes: B alpha_p has infinitesimal pi1; internal sheaves not conflated with external proshape groups Task aliases: B.3.15. Contributor status detail: Known with checked deduction.

statement: Let $Y$ be a regular separated scheme of finite type over $\Z$. For each morphism $f:X\to Y$ of separated finite type $\Z$-schemes there is a canonical rational bivariant orientation $[f]$, uniquely characterized by $[f]([Y])=[X]$. For irreducible $X,Y$ it has degree $-\dim_YX$ and gives, in the relative dimension grading, \[ f^*:\mathrm{CH}_k(Y)_\Q\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}_{k+\dim_\Z X-\dim_\Z Y}(X)_\Q. \] It is compatible with proper pushforward, flat pullback and refined Gysin maps; compositions of orientations agree whenever the intermediate target is also regular. In particular $X$ need not be regular, and $f$ need not be flat or lci. The coefficient field $\Q$ and the finite type hypotheses are retained.
where_proved: sections/part_b.tex, label thm:B3-chow-pullback, statement 8.45, PDF p. 92
notes: X need not be regular or f lci; Q coefficients and separated finite type Z scope retained Task aliases: B.3.23. Contributor status detail: Known with checked deduction.

statement: Every generically reduced noetherian quasi-excellent $\Q$-scheme admits a finite sequence of blowups with regular centres, disjoint from the inverse image of its regular locus, whose final scheme is regular. The construction is functorial for regular morphisms, up to omitting empty blowups. For a separated finite type scheme $X$ over any field $k$, a nowhere dense closed $Z\subset X$, and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, there are a finite extension $k'/k$ of degree prime to $\ell$ and a proper surjective generically finite alteration $X'\to X$ of degree prime to $\ell$, with $X'$ smooth quasi-projective over $k'$ and inverse image of $Z$ the support of a strict normal-crossings divisor. The alteration assertion does not assert a birational resolution in arbitrary characteristic and dimension.
where_proved: sections/part_b.tex, label thm:B3-resolution, statement 8.46, PDF p. 93
notes: No unrestricted birational resolution in positive characteristic is claimed Task aliases: B.PM.resolution. Contributor status detail: Known with checked deduction.

statement: Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of constant codimension $c$ between regular noetherian schemes, and let $\Lambda=\Z/n\Z$ with $n$ invertible on $X$. The cycle-class Gysin morphism is an isomorphism \[ Ri^!\Lambda\simeq\Lambda(-c)[-2c]. \] In particular $\mathcal H^q_Z(\Lambda)$ vanishes for $q\ne2c$; in degree $2c$ it is $i_*\Lambda(-c)$.
where_proved: sections/part_b.tex, label thm:B3-purity, statement 8.47, PDF p. 93
notes: Both source and target regular; codimension c gives twist -c and shift -2c Task aliases: B.PM.purity. Contributor status detail: Known with checked deduction.

statement: In a Cartesian square with $f:T\to S$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated and $g:S'\to S$ a regular morphism of noetherian schemes, let $f':T'\to S'$ and $g':T'\to T$ be the projections. For every \'etale $\Z/n\Z$-sheaf $F$ on $T$, where $n$ is invertible on $S$, the base-change map is an isomorphism \[ g^*Rf_*F\simeq Rf'_*g'^*F. \]
where_proved: sections/part_b.tex, label thm:B3-regular-bc, statement 8.48, PDF p. 94

notes: Regular map between noetherian schemes need not be finite type Task aliases: B.PM.regularbasechange. Contributor status detail: Known with checked deduction.

statement: Let $X$ be a noetherian excellent $\Z[1/n]$-scheme with a dimension function $\delta$, and put $\Lambda=\Z/n\Z$. There is a normalized potential dualizing complex $K_{X,\delta}$, unique with its normalization, belonging to $D^b_{\mathrm{ctf}}(X_{\mathrm{\acute et}},\Lambda)$. The functor $D_K=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,K_{X,\delta})$ preserves $D^b_c$, and for every $M\in D^b_c$ the canonical map \[ M\longrightarrow D_KD_KM \] is an isomorphism. The complex has finite quasi-injective dimension if and only if $X$ has finite Krull dimension; in that case it is also a dualizing complex in the SGA~5 sense.
where_proved: sections/part_b.tex, label thm:B3-local-biduality, statement 8.49, PDF p. 94
notes: Dimension function required; finite quasi-injective dimension iff finite Krull dimension Task aliases: B.PM.biduality. Contributor status detail: Known with checked deduction.

statement: Let $X$ be noetherian quasi-excellent, $f:Y\to X$ of finite type, and $F$ a constructible \'etale $\Z/n\Z$-sheaf on $Y$, with $n$ invertible on $X$. Then every $R^qf_*F$ is constructible and $R^qf_*F=0$ for all sufficiently large $q$. Equivalently $Rf_*$ preserves bounded constructible complexes. No properness assumption on $f$ or finite Krull dimension assumption on $X$ is needed in this theorem.
where_proved: sections/part_b.tex, label thm:B3-finiteness, statement 8.50, PDF p. 94
notes: No properness or finite Krull-dimension assumption; invertible torsion coefficients Task aliases: B.PM.finiteness. Contributor status detail: Known with checked deduction.

statement: Let $X$ be noetherian quasi-excellent with dimension function $\delta$, let $f:Y\to X$ be affine of finite type, and let $F$ be a constructible \'etale $\Z/n\Z$-sheaf with $n$ invertible on $X$. Set $\delta_Y(y)=\delta(f(y))+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(f(y))}\kappa(y)$ and $\delta(F)=\sup\{\delta_Y(y):F_{\bar y}\ne0\}$. Then \[ \sup\{\delta(x):(R^qf_*F)_{\bar x}\ne0\}\leq\delta(F)-q. \] For an affine variety of dimension $d$ over a separably closed field, this implies $H^q(Y,F)=0$ for $q>d$.
where_proved: sections/part_b.tex, label thm:B3-affine-cd, statement 8.51, PDF p. 95

statement: For a proper holomorphic map $f:X\to Y$ of complex analytic spaces and a coherent analytic $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$, every $R^qf_*F$ is coherent. In particular cohomology of a coherent sheaf on a compact complex space is finite dimensional.

statement: Let $K$ be complete for a nontrivial rank-one nonarchimedean valuation. On an affinoid rigid space $X=\operatorname{Sp}A$, finite $A$-modules correspond to coherent analytic sheaves and have no higher cohomology. For every proper map of rigid $K$-spaces, all higher direct images of coherent sheaves are coherent. If $R$ is the valuation ring, taking generic fibre induces an equivalence between quasi-paracompact admissible formal $R$-schemes localized at admissible formal blowups and quasi-paracompact quasi-separated rigid $K$-spaces.
where_proved: sections/part_b.tex, label thm:B3-rigid, statement 8.53, PDF p. 95

statement: The reference is to SGA~2, and its proposed finiteness statements cannot all be recorded as affirmative theorems. In particular SGA~2, Expos\'e XIII, Conjecture 1.1 is false: a local cohomology module of a finite module over a regular noetherian ring need not have finitely generated $I$-annihilator. A precise positive local Lefschetz conclusion is that every noetherian local complete-intersection ring of dimension at least four is parafactorial. Consequently a noetherian local complete-intersection ring that is factorial at every prime of height at most three is factorial.
where_proved: sections/part_b.tex, label thm:B3-sga2, statement 8.54, PDF p. 96

statement: Let $X,Y_1,\ldots,Y_m$ be smooth projective fourfolds over $k$, and suppose $D^2_\ell(Y_i)$ holds. Suppose algebraic correspondences $a_i\in\operatorname{CH}^4(X\times Y_i)_\Q$ and $b_i\in\operatorname{CH}^4(Y_i\times X)_\Q$ satisfy \[ \sum_i(b_i)_*(a_i)_*=\operatorname{id} \quad\hbox{on }H^4(X_{\bar k},\Q_\ell(2)). \] Then $D^2_\ell(X)$ holds. In particular this applies to a generically finite surjective morphism from any $Y_i$ to $X$.

statement: Let $X$ be a smooth projective fourfold over $k$, let $Z\subset X$ be a smooth closed center of positive codimension on every component, and let $f:W=\operatorname{Bl}_ZX\to X$. Then $D^2_\ell(W)$ holds if and only if $D^2_\ell(X)$ holds.

statement: Let $\operatorname{char}k\ne3$ and let \[ F=\{z_0^3+\cdots+z_5^3=0\}\subset\mathbf P^5_k. \] For every $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, numerical and $\ell$-adic homological equivalence agree for all cycles on $F$ with rational coefficients. The same holds for any smooth projective $k$-form of $F$. Together with Ancona's numerical Hodge theorem for $F$, this places these fourfolds in the homological-positivity class of Proposition~\ref{prop:B1b-criterion}.

statement: The maps \[ D\longmapsto \exp D=\sum_{j\geq0}\frac{D^j}{j!},\qquad u\longmapsto \log u=\sum_{j\geq1}\frac{(-1)^{j+1}}j(u-1)^j \] are mutually inverse bijections between nilpotent $K$-derivations of $A$ and $K$-algebra automorphisms $u$ for which $u-1$ is nilpotent in $\operatorname{End}_K(A)$. Both sums are finite. The nilpotency indices of $D$ and $\exp D-1$ coincide.

statement: Let $I\subset A$ be an ideal with $I^m=0$, where $m\geq1$. Exponential is a bijection from \[ \mathfrak d_I= \{D\in\operatorname{Der}_K(A):D(I^k)\subset I^{k+1} \text{ for every }k\geq0\} \] to \[ U_I=\{u\in\operatorname{Aut}_K(A):u(I)=I, \ \operatorname{gr}_I(u)=1\}. \] Its inverse is the polynomial logarithm. Here $I^0=A$ and $\operatorname{gr}_I(A)=\bigoplus_{k\geq0}I^k/I^{k+1}$. This is the valid replacement of the last corollary of 68/046.

statement: For $u\in\operatorname{Aut}_K(A)$ let $J=(u(a)-a:a\in A)\subset A$. For every $n\geq0$, \[ u\text{ has differential order at most }n \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad J^{n+1}=0. \] Suppose more generally that $I^m=0$ and $u$ induces the identity on $A/I$. Then $u(I)=I$ and it induces an $(A/I)$-linear automorphism $\gamma:I/I^2\to I/I^2$. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item $u=\exp D$ for a nilpotent $K$-derivation $D$ of $A$; \item $u-1$ is nilpotent on the $K$-module $A$; \item $\gamma-1$ is nilpotent on the $(A/I)$-module $I/I^2$. \end{enumerate} If $(\gamma-1)^r=0$, then one valid bound is \[ (u-1)^{m+(r-1)m(m-1)/2}=0. \] In particular this characterizes exactly which differential automorphisms are exponentials, by taking $I=J$. The other differential automorphisms are exactly those with non-unipotent action on $J/J^2$, where unipotent here requires a uniform nilpotence bound.
where_proved: sections/part_c.tex, label C-differential, statement 9.3, PDF p. 98
notes: C.1(b); arbitrary Q-algebras and modules

statement: A differential automorphism need not be an exponential of a nilpotent derivation. On $A=\Q[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$, the automorphism $u(\epsilon)=2\epsilon$ has differential order one and is not such an exponential. The assertion in 68/045 that $u$ automatically acts identically on $\operatorname{gr}_J(A)$ is also false. For any $\Q$-vector space $V$, the square-zero algebra $\Q\oplus V$ has all $\Q$-algebra automorphisms of the form $1\oplus T$, with $T\in\operatorname{GL}_{\Q}(V)$. All are differential of order at most one; precisely those for which $T-1$ is uniformly nilpotent are exponentials of nilpotent derivations. Thus no finite dimensional or semisimple description of the remaining automorphisms is available without additional hypotheses.

statement: Let $M,N$ be arbitrary $K$-modules, let $u\in\operatorname{End}_K(M)$ and $v\in\operatorname{End}_K(N)$ be locally nilpotent, and let $f:M\to N$ be $K$-linear. Then \[ f\exp(u)=\exp(v)f\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad fu=vf. \] The exponentials are pointwise finite, mutually invertible linear maps.

statement: For any $K$-module functor $\mathcal M$: \begin{enumerate} \item The ordinary exponential map \[ \{u\in\mathscr E(K):u\text{ nilpotent}\} \longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathcal O,\mathscr E^\times) \] is injective. Its image consists exactly of actions $\rho$ satisfying both of the following explicit conditions: there is a single integer $m$ with $(\rho_R(\lambda)-1)^m=0$ for every $R$ and $\lambda\in R$; and their polynomial logarithms define an $\mathcal O$-linear natural map $L:\mathcal O\to\mathscr E$. Thus this exponential map is bijective exactly when every action satisfies these two conditions. \item The formal exponential map \[ \mathscr E(K)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{gr}}(\mathcal N,\mathscr E^\times) \] has image exactly the formal actions $\rho$ for which each $\rho_R(\lambda)-1$ is nilpotent in $\mathscr E(R)$ and the natural map $L_R(\lambda)=\log\rho_R(\lambda)$ extends to an $\mathcal O$-linear natural map $\mathcal O\to\mathscr E$. Nilpotence bounds in this assertion may depend on $(R,\lambda)$. Its fibres, when nonempty, are translates of \[ H(\mathcal M)=\{w\in\mathscr E(K): \lambda w_R=0\text{ for every }R\text{ and every } \lambda\in\operatorname{Nil}(R)\}. \] Consequently formal exponential is bijective exactly when $H(\mathcal M)=0$ and every formal action meets the displayed logarithm and extension conditions. \end{enumerate} These criteria apply to every module functor; they require no quasicoherence assumption.

statement: Let $M$ be any $K$-module and $\mathcal M(R)=R\otimes_K M$. Formal actions of $\widehat{\mathbb G}_a=\mathcal N$ on $\mathcal M$ are uniquely the $\bar e_u$ for $u\in\operatorname{End}_K(M)$. Ordinary actions of $\mathbb G_a=\mathcal O$ are uniquely the $e_u$ for locally nilpotent endomorphisms $u$ of $M$. Consequently the ordinary map with domain only uniformly nilpotent endomorphisms is bijective exactly when every locally nilpotent endomorphism of $M$ is uniformly nilpotent. Finite generation of $M$ suffices for this last property but is not asserted to be necessary. The ordinary classification is stated in \cite[Chapter VIII, Example 2.1 and footnote 1, p.~113]{MilneAGS}.

statement: For $f,g\in\R^{(G)}_+$, \[ \sup_{f'\sim f}\sum_x f'(x)g(x)=|f,g|, \qquad \|f*g\|_\infty\leq|f,g|. \] An inner product achieves its rearrangement maximum precisely when every positive superlevel set of one factor is comparable by inclusion with every positive superlevel set of the other. Consequently $(f,g)$ is pr\'etass\'e precisely when there exists $s\in G$ such that the superlevel sets of $f$ and $\delta_s*\check g$ together form a chain. Moreover $f'\prec f$ is equivalent to $|f',h|\leq|f,h|$ for every $h\in\R^{(G)}_+$.

statement: Let $S\subset\R^{(G)}_+$ be convolution stable and suppose that for every positive integer $k\leq|G|$ it contains an indicator $1_{A_k}$ with $|A_k|=k$. The following are equivalent: \begin{enumerate} \item Every pair in $S\times S$ is tass\'e. \item For every $n\geq2$, $f_i\in S$ and $f_i'\prec f_i$ imply $f_1'*\cdots*f_n'\prec f_1*\cdots*f_n$. \item Condition $K$ holds: under those hypotheses, $\|f_1'*\cdots*f_n'\|_\infty \leq\|f_1*\cdots*f_n\|_\infty$. \end{enumerate} For the implication from (3) to (1), it suffices to assume only the three-factor instances with third factor $1_{A_k}$. Thus the missing hypothesis in Lead L8 is a genuine convolution-majorization property; chain closure and pairwise optimal suprema alone do not supply it.

statement: Interpret ${}_2G$ as the subset $T=\{t\in G:t^2=e\}$ with the multiplication inherited from $G$, and retain exactly the draft axioms just stated, without adding cardinality completeness. For a finite or arbitrary discrete group $G$, data satisfying these axioms and $i:T\simeq\ker\rho$ exist if and only if $T$ is a subgroup of $G$, equivalently if and only if every two involutions commute. The construction can have a surjective $\rho$ and at least one nonzero cone. In particular, within the abelian category every finite and every discrete group admits a system in this literal sense.
